evidence_ledger.bottleneck: A funding call is 3-8 pages of eligibility rules, scope language, and priorities. Matching it to a faculty member means holding the call's constraints in your head while reading someone's publication list and deciding whether the fit is real or superficial. It's a comparison task across two long, messy documents, done 60 times per call, and the officer's attention degrades after the first fifteen.

evidence_ledger.hot_take_text: The remaining errors are near-misses on interdisciplinary faculty: someone whose work genuinely spans two areas gets a middling score in both instead of a high score for the combination, because each step evaluates fit one dimension at a time. The checker doesn't help here - the reason is supported, it's just underweight. Hot take: every agent in this pipeline had to earn its place in the metric, not the diagram. Three of the four steps moved nDCG or the constraint-violation count; the fourth (the removed advocate) moved neither and we cut it even though it made the architecture diagram look more thorough. The lesson we're taking forward: add the step, measure, and be willing to delete it the same day if the number doesn't move - 'it seems like it should help' is how you end up paying 35% more for a loop.

Our hot take: verification passes built to catch wrong tone won't catch wrong silence — if the real signal lives outside the artifact you're reviewing (ticket history, not ticket text), no amount of re-reading the same ticket harder will find it. The next version needs a tool call out to ticket history, not a better prompt.
